key_insight: The time gap between two drop impacts controls how two generated vortex rings merge, deform, or remain separate, with four distinct interaction regimes emerging as \u0394t increases.
engineering_relevance: For drop-based mixing and impact-driven flow systems, precise timing of adjacent drops is crucial to achieve predictable vortex formation and uniform fluid mixing.
method: Two water drops were released onto a deep water pool with controlled impact time difference \u0394t.
Particle image velocimetry (PIV) was used to track the time evolution of the resulting vortex rings.
The observed behaviors were grouped into four interaction regimes based on \u0394t.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports experimentally measured vortex-ring evolution for multiple \u0394t ranges, identifying symmetric merging, asymmetric/incomplete merging, no merging, and isolated ring evolution.
watch_item: The regime boundaries are experiment-specific and may shift with drop size, impact speed, fluid properties, or pool depth, so direct transfer to other setups should be validated.
paper_title: Interaction of vortex rings generated by two unsynchronised drop impacts
